text_fidelity_a:
Creative Sound Blaster Roar 2 Portable NFC Bluetooth Speaker with aptX/AAC (Black) I am an audiophile but I always take into account the nature of the product that I am looking at or listening to. One cannot possibly expect a $99 portable bluetooth speaker to have legitimate audiophile sound. In this case, we're talking about the Creative Sound Blaster Roar. And that assertion is not in any way a knock on this product. I bought one a few days ago and I like it and am quite happy with the purchase for a variety of reasons. The main reason I like it is because the sound it produces is GOOD. That sound is not great nor is it bad. Perhaps the worst credible thing you might say about the sound is simply that it is FINE. When I consider the size of the unit (and the size of the very small speakers it contains) and the cost, I judge the sound to be GOOD. You are not going to get Martin Logan or Definitive Technology sound out of the Roar, plain and simple. Nor will you get super sound out of any of the other competitive products such as the Bose or JBL, etc. I think they all produce generally good sound for the money. The best and smartest thing a buyer can do is perhaps go to
Best Buy or any of the other retailers who carry such units and give them all a listen and look at the features they offer and then buy the one that meets your needs in terms of both sound quality and features. Having said that, for me the Roar has more features than any of the
competing units. That is simply fact and not opinion. Most of the products that are in this category seem to be made well but in my opinion, the Roar seems to be made just a little sturdier. I haven't tested that notion by dropping my Roar on the floor but in my hands it simply feels
more robust. Back to the sound question.....since I seriously doubt that many users of portable bluetooth speakers plan on doing serious
listening that entails sitting in a quite room and doing nothing but listening intently to these little portable speakers, consider how they will actually be used. Most people are playing them as background music while they are doing other things such as sitting on the beach or
cooking on the grill or in the kitchen, etc. Critical listening ain't happening here. So let's not talk about sound imaging or speaker spatiality etc. That said, for me, I don't like speakers that have a bass response that overwhelms everything else. I want a more natural sound, One that is

more balanced to my ear. Because of that, I will gravitate towards something like the Roar. If you are one who wants more bass, then you will assuredly better like the sound of any Bose product as they have made a fortune producing bass heavy products for the last 50 years. Again, for me, the features are a big deal and the Roar excels inn that regard. I won't waste your time talking about them as you can look such things up just as easily. And price is a big deal to me. The Roar 1 can be had for $99 now.... so I bought one. The Bose is $299 the last time I checked,...three times the cost of the Roar. So simply put, I loved the price of the Roar, the feature list is unmatched, it feels like military grade construction and lastly, I thought the sound was GOOD. That's why I bought it.
text_fidelity_b: Creative Sound Blaster Roar 2 Portable NFC Bluetooth Speaker with aptX/AAC (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
HP ENVY 13-13.99 Inches Thin Laptop w/ Fingerprint Reader, 4K Touchscreen, Intel Core i7-8565U, NVIDIA GeForce MX250 Graphics, 16GB SDRAM, 512GB SSD, Windows 10 Home (13-aq0044nr, Natural Silver) These are probably the last words that come to mind when thinking of a laptop, but this Ultrabook earns its name and then some in every way, because anyone who sees you using this will be BESIDE themselves, and I mean SICK, with Envy. This thang is FIYAH!!!!!!!!!!

Let's start with the unboxing: it arrives in a sleek, black box with a beautiful photo of the laptop on its cover, and when you open it, you are awed by the pristine, silver gleaming contraption inside. When you pick it up and gently unwrap it from its plastic film, you are wowed by how both light and elegant it is in your hands; how something so small can contain your life, and then you can't wait to start filling it up with it. You open the lid and lift the mesh cover protecting the keys; you notice the setup leaflet and take out the power cord, plug her in and turn her on.

From there, Cortana takes over, guiding you through the setup! By voice command! Very Jason Bourne. You set up your fingerprint log in, sign in to your accounts and then once everything is registered, off into the wild wild web you go. The first thing you'll notice is how FAST this baby is, the gentle whir of the machine as she takes you off to the farthest reaches of the world if you check out the 4K resolution by looking at the Planet Earth series. It's enough to bring tears to your eyes. You'll be mesmerized by the rhythmic clicking of the keys as you go to your favorite websites and download/install your must-have apps and programs; you will find yourself looking down at the keyboard and smiling as if you've been enchanted by a new lover, and you HAVE!

I had been looking for a new computer because I've got this ollllld slooooooooow, 4GB RAM dinosaur of an 15" laptop that I bought used in a dire emergency because I accidentally cracked the screen on my Toshiba. The "Gorilla glass" on this is so beautiful that I don't even want to TOUCH it, even though the touch screen is flawless, like you are on a tablet.

The keyboard is perfectly sized and responsive; there is just so much here for me to continue to explore but I am damn near breathless as I write this review because it is simply that exceptional, stunning. I have had some graphic design programs that I wanted to use but was waiting until I got something new so it would have the capacity to rock out, and I can't wait to get started. Where this HAS been incredible for me is Traktor and music programs. No more worrying about lag and staticky mixing because of system overload. This has all the memory and SSD space that you will need, and its ports will more than accommodate any other gadgets you need to connect to it. The sound is exemplary, with the Bang & Olufsen speakers.

This is the Ultrabook that every entrepreneur or very lucky student should have; it is the answer and perhaps even a juggernaut to the Macbook. I've certainly learned that just one POWERFUL Ultrabook is WORTH the investment rather than having to replace a tired ass notebook every few years. I prefer large screens so 13 inches has never appealed to me, but this right here has ROCKED. MY. WORLD. I don't wanna go anywhere without it, not even the shower. LOL

You have just got to see for yourself.
text_fidelity_b: HP ENVY 13-13.99 Inches Thin Laptop w/ Fingerprint Reader, 4K Touchscreen, Intel Core i7-8565U, NVIDIA GeForce MX250 Graphics, 16GB SDRAM, 512GB SSD, Windows 10 Home (13-aq0044nr, Natural Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
TV Antenna, Digital TV Antenna for Smart TV Indoor, Strong Magnetic Base for Easy Installation, 360°& Long Range Reception for HDTV Channels-Support All Tv's-10ft Long Cables Our house is about 40 miles east of the local CBS and FOX affiliate's transmitter, and maybe 10 miles the same direction from the others. The TV is beside an east wall with large front windows. We had been using one of the flat amplified antennas, and it just couldn't get the distant station. I don't know if the signals didn't want to go through too many walls, or if the high voltage electric transmission line running along the east edge of our front yard was responsible.

When I installed this antenna, I still couldn't get CBS. With the nice long piece of coax attached to it, I experimented with various places. The window was a no go, no matter where it was placed, giving my power line hypothesis some points. Holding it high its full distance to the west worked. We are lucky enough to have a tall bookshelf there, so I stuck it to a metal bookend on top of it. Success!

text_fidelity_a: APC UPS 1500VA UPS Battery Backup and Surge Protector, BX1500M Backup Battery Power Supply, AVR, Dataline Protection If you have electronics, you need a ups battery backup. For years, I have used a backup to prevent loss due to power surges. With a backup, if you are in the middle of working on something on your computer (like a thesis), when the power goes out, it gives you enough time to save your work and shut down the computer safely. In our household, we have 2 desktops, 2 laptops, 4 tvs/monitors, xbox one, ps3, speaker systems, digital piano and more. These are very expensive pieces of equipment, especially the piano. We also have all of our cabling in the garage and keep that on a ups battery backup too. The only thing I don't have on a backup, is the gaming computer. Now it is on a backup. Makes life a little less discouraging if you lose a piece of electronics during a power surge. By the way, it is compact, but it is still pretty heavy. It comes with half surge protected outlets and 5 power/surge protected outlets, cable connection in and out, usb protection and data protection.

text_fidelity_a:
TomTom Via 1525SE 5 Inch GPS Navigation Device with Free Traffic, Free Maps of the US, Advanced Lane Guidance and Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions Of the three main GPS receiver manufacturers - Garmin, TomTom and Magellan - I have had the most success with TomTom devices. My first GPS was a TomTom and it served me well for years until the map outgrew the memory. I was excited to have the opportunity to try this one; so far, it has been a good unit, though I do not care for the menu system.

This is a larger unit than the original one I had, upgrading from a 4.3" to a 6". I like the screen real estate. For all that screen space, TomTom has made good use of it, maximizing the visible map and keeping the interface clean and uncluttered. One area where I am slightly disappointed, though, is in the speed display which is a little small - it's good to keep it out of the way but it's a little smaller than I like and it a bit harder to read. If you use your GPS for watching your speed, this could be a problem.

Navigation is easy. I like the way this unit routes me to my destination yet does not nag me when I go off the chosen route. Others I have used (including my old TomTom) would badger me to make a U-turn for a while before deciding that there was another way to get where I was going. This unit does make that point sometimes, but it also is smart enough to reroute when I have multiple similar routes.

The biggest plus for this unit (and it seems to be a TomTom thing) is that the voice very clearly enunciates without distortion or the unit buzzing. I have had this issue with every other unit of every other brand, but my old TomTom was clear and understandible even at higher volumes. Since this one is the same, I believe TomTom has a better understanding of how to build a unit that sounds right.

Navigating from work to home is usually a straight shot down the interstate for 40+ miles and a little bit of backroads. To test, I instead took a long, out-of-the-way route that I use when there is heavy traffic volume. Knowing it would try to put me on the interstate, I set the farthest point as a first leg, then set it to take me home from there. The route it chose was actually only slightly different than the one I had chosen already, and the difference was that I accounted for rush hour traffic.

Speaking of traffic... This unit gathers traffic data without relying on mobile data. I greatly prefer this to having to run an app on my phone and letting it gather traffic info from online. So far I have not had it report a reroute due to traffic; I will come back here and update when it does.

The main complaint I have about this GPS is the menu system. WIth TomTom's older units, the menu system was fairly traditional and was smiliar to that of a PC application menu system (sorta). The new interface has a scrolling row of icons that lead to more icons. I am not a fan of this type of interface and is the one thing I would change about this unit if I could.

When this unit is first powered on and set up it downloads a hefty amount of data to update the map. This is unavoidable, unfortunately. Do not be discouraged by this - it will be up to date and ready to go when it finishes.

I have not had any real issues with this unit so far. It works well and I like how it navigates. I don't like the menu system and find it very awkward, but it gets me where I want to go with little fuss.
text_fidelity_b: TomTom Via 1525SE 5 Inch GPS Navigation Device with Free Traffic, Free Maps of the US, Advanced Lane Guidance and Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions

Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black Fortunately I bought this at a much cheaper price at $16 instead of the current price as of this writing at $27. There are lots of comparable wireless vertical ergonomic mice less than $27 that also include recharging and cool LED lights. Although it's a decent ergonomic vertical mouse, there are some legitimate gripes with this mouse after months of use so now I'm looking to try a different brand of vertical mouse.

The 2.4Ghz range is pretty bad. I found this out later down the road when I had to switch the USB dongle to a port on the back of my computer. At first I thought my batteries were low (or some dirt interfering with optical sensor) because my mouse cursor would stagger on and off as a moved cursor across screen. That was really frustrating not only for browsing but games. When I put the dongle closer to the front of computer it worked much better.

Now onto the batteries. This may be good or bad depending on preference but it uses AAA batteries. Although replacing batteries seems like an inconvenience, if you have a mouse with a built-in rechargeable lithium ion battery and the batteries go bad or defective then you would have to trash the whole mouse instead of just replacing the batteries.

There is a separate top button on the mouse for DPI toggle (800/1200/1600) but I can't tell what mode it is in unless I move the mouse across the screen every time I toggle it so it is kind of inconvenient. Would be nice so you can visually see the dpi on the mouse or on screen.

Overall, the mouse feel good upon touching it. The texture on the mouse is not glossy plastic but has a slight comfy texture on it. My personal gripe with the ergonomics is it feels a bit narrow and the hand does not feel relaxed. I think the culprit is the thumb rest position feels like it is a bit upwards causes your thumb to squeeze inward instead of relaxing. So I try not to point or put my thumb in the default thumb rest but more below the thumb rest or even slight bend my thumb so it's not straight and stiff.

Kingston 64GB DataTraveler Elite G2 Black Metal Casing Fast 180MB/s R, 70MB/W USB 3.1 Flash Drive with LED light indicator (DTEG2/64GB) This is an unremarkable USB drive, with unexciting performance, for an unattractive price. (That's pretty much it for the substance of the review.)

I do my tests on a pretty fast computer with tons of memory, and an SSD system drive, while I'm doing nothing else on the computer, so no system resource constraints should affect the results. I test writes from SSD to USB, and reads in the other direction. I also use a set of 2GB test files, so that I get true results (small files can give misleading results).

I saw writes to the USB drive going between 4.5 and 8 MB/s, which is really pretty slow. I can get 16+ consistently on a little Lexar 32GB drive I have lying around. And a quick look in Amazon shows that I can find much faster USB3 drives for a bit less or a bit more, promising about 5x the write performance.

Finally, the form factor is terrible. This is a big fat ugly drive, you can get higher capacity and much better performance in slim little drives, including nano-drive size products.

Bottom line, it's ok, but I can't recommend it.

text_fidelity_a:
iHome iAVS16 Bedside Speaker with Alexa Built In, Bluetooth, and USB Charging, Now Supports Spotify by Voice This is a pretty mixed review of an interesting concept that is pretty good right now, but has the potential to be great in the near future. At the current price of about $150, this is ok+ based on the following criteria:

Sound Quality: 2.5-3 stars
For the size, it's ok
When reviewing for sound quality, I compare speakers (and headphones) to comparably sized items, based on speakers I currently or previously have owned. I take price range *somewhat* into account (I don't expect $15 headphones to sound like $500 ones), but for anything over $100, I use the full range from the cheapest stuff I have, to my favorite brand, Bose.
So with that in mind, I have a portable wireless Bose speaker that is smaller and acts as the "5" on the scale.
The sound on this can get loud enough to not distort and still fill a smallish room or normal bedroom fine. The treble and bass are ok, though the higher ranges are tinny and the bass lacks depth. Overall sound from high to low and throughout the mid range lack definition. It's good enough for very casual background listening and for podcasts.

Alexa Feature: 4 stars
I have an iPhone and think Alexa has quite a bit more understanding and skill than Siri. When asked questions, from simple stuff like "what's the weather" to more complicated stuff like "I'm hungry. What can I make in half an hour?", the answers and follow-up questions are highly intuitive and thorough. Does she get everything all the time? No. But she does a much better job than Siri.

User-Friendliness: 2.5 stars
I didn't like the process of figuring out how this works, particularly the part of pairing with more than one device and also Having to use an app to make most of it work. It was a clunky, irritating process that more or less stayed that way every time I wanted to use this thing, especially for listening to music. It should be able to just play from your iTunes through the iTunes app and bluetooth, and instead, I was only able to make it play iTunes though Their App, which sucks when it comes to my music. And that brings us to the App..

App: 2 stars
No. Just no. Bluetooth exists for a reason, and if a speaker has bluetooth, you should be able to just pair and play. I had to use the app to play from my iTunes, and because I have a very specific way of organizing things, I was incredibly annoyed that something didn't translate, and my music was disorganized and basically impossible to search for with this app. Instead of being able to play what I want from one of my playlist subfolders, it disregarded my way of organizing things, and I ended up giving up. If I can't listen to my stuff easily with this, then like 75% of the reason to use this disappears, leaving me with an expensive alarm clock with weather report, recipe ideas, and some cool internet stuff. That's cool, but it's quite incomplete for what I need, and what I suspect many people want.

tl;dr version: sound is mediocre but doable, app is bad, Alexa is super clever and smart, and the experience has a lot of frustrating aspects.
text_fidelity_b: iHome iAVS16 Bedside Speaker with Alexa Built In, Bluetooth, and USB Charging, Now Supports Spotify by Voice

This charges using the type C cord in a few hours.

PICTURE
The picture is decent. It is not like watching an expensive bluray or TV screen, but it is fine for close up watching.

OPERATION
I have had no issues operating this. It is pretty easy and the set up is not difficult to adjust.

SOUND
That is where we lose a star. Even at the highest setting of 20 this is so quiet that if I run fans in the summer, it is hard to hear with the player right in front of me. Headphones would solve that, but I don't always want to wear them.

THE BOTTOM LINE

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. If the sound was a little bit louder and better, I would like this more. As it is it is still okay.

text_fidelity_a:
Yooeur 12X50 Monocular Telescope-Compact Short-range Spotting Scope-Waterproof Fog Dust proof- Single Hand Focus My wife loves birdwatching and our teenage son enjoys stargazing so we have an assortment of binoculars and inexpensive telescopes. Before this monocular I had never used one and even though I have not had it very long at all I am already very pleased with it. Though it is ideal for bird watching and field work, it also will work as an amateur telescope.

At roughly 7" long, this monocular is large enough to be usable but small enough to fit in a coat pocket or even in a briefcase. It comes in a nice, nylon-weave carrying pouch that even has a belt loop so carrying it into the field is easy and does not take up extra room. It also has a holding strap much like a camcorder does so it can be held more securely. It has a small metal tripod suitable for setting up on a desk or table. It’s not a big tripod - the legs extend to 7.5" - but is works well if you are recording or are seated and need a steady hand. Finally, it includes a microfiber cleaning cloth in the box for wiping the lenses safely without scratching them.

This is a waterproof monocular and everything about it showcases that. There are two rubberized caps for either end that cover the lenses and keep out moisture and dust when not in use. These are physically attached to the barrel (one by a rubber flap and one by a nylon cord) so there is no issue with losing the caps. Most of the barrel is rubberized as well except for the focus knob assembly and where it attaches.

I used it to focus on the tree line behind the house (roughly 30 yards away) and was very pleased with how sharp and clear I was able to get the image. From the front of the house I was able to focus on the stop sign at the end of the street and had no issue with getting fine edge detail even at a distance of roughly a football field. The focus is very smooth and easy to adjust and getting the image in perfect focus is not the least bit difficult.

Though I enjoy cameras and optical equipment and I have learned a good bit about optical equipment I am a far cry from being an expert, so I took this monocular to work and approached two teammates who are very well-versed in optics, photography and astronomy and I asked them to look it over and give me their honest opinion. Both of them examined it and expressed their approval. They both said similar things about it: the image through this monocular is very bright and clear, the focus is very smooth and it seems to be very well made. They both made a comment about the lens and that it was very good due to not having a darkened coating.

One of my teammates told me to try looking at the stars with it. I had not really considered this but knew this would be an excellent test for it so I went outside after dark and pointed it skyward. Though I can definitely see more detail through a dedicated telescope, I was able to make out some of the larger surface detail on the moon including the high point in the middle of a crater. I was hindered by the fact that it is a full moon right now so I will have to try again this weekend during the eclipse. I then picked out a planet and looked at it through the monocular. Though it is a little tough to make out, I know I found Jupiter as I could see three of the moons as bright spots not visible to the naked eye (I have looked at it through a telescope so I recognize it from seeing it already). Finally I discovered a cluster of stars I could not see without magnification. This monocular is certainly not as good as a dedicated telescope but it is sufficient when camping and it eliminates the need to pack a big, bulky telescope unless you want to see more detail.

This is a great tool for use in the field. It has very good range, the image is bright and clear and it even is sufficient for stargazing should you choose to use it for everything on the road. Great product!

text_fidelity_a:
Soundcore Wakey Bluetooth Speaker Powered by Anker with Alarm Clock, Stereo Sound, FM Radio, White Noise, QI Wireless Charger with 7.5W Charging for iPhone and 10W for Samsung I ordered the 'Soundcore Wakey Bluetooth Speaker Powered by Anker with Alarm Clock, Stereo Sound, FM Radio, White Noise, QI Wireless Charger with 7.5W Charging for iPhone and 10W for Samsung' for review and would like to share some of my thoughts after a few weeks.

First off, this thing is actually pretty amazing. The build quality is nice and aesthetically it looks clean. The sound quality is nice but not phenomenal. However for how small it is, it does produce decent sound and for a bedside alarm clock it does quite well. The wireless charging works great for my Galaxy Note 8 (and does in fact Fast-Charge) however there have been a couple nights to where my phone was not charged the next morning. The fast charger also works with my wireless earbuds which I attached an image showing the charge light on the Wakey, and the wireless earbuds case indicating charging. However for the wireless earbud charging, it does take some precise positioning to get them to charge. I noticed in other review that others weren't happy with the bright display light with no way to adjust it any dimmer than the lowest setting, however they must have updated that with a firmware update (which was super easy to do) as I had no issues with the display being too bright at night. I use the auto adjust setting which seems to work quite well as far as I can tell. Also I love the sleep mode sounds that you can adjust several (or just one) sound volumes to create your own personalized preference. I do wish that there were more sound options but the ones they provide are acceptable. I also wish that you could download and install more alarm sounds. Bluetooth connectivity is super quick and have never once had an issue with pairing it up to my phone. Really the ONLY issue I have with the Wakey is that to get the sleep mode sounds going, you need to connect with the app, and via Bluetooth connect to the device. No big deal right? Well my concern is that you will need to keep it connected for this feature to work. This means you will be connected to the Wakey ALL night and this kind of bugs me. It's just kind of creepy that the Wakey is connected to your phone all night while you sleep. I wish there was a way to just play your favorite white noise sleep sound by pressing a button on the Wakey device without having to always connect and stay connected to the app and your phone. The other gripe is that the plug design is huge and makes it so that I have had to move my nightstand further way from the wall to use it. Other than those two gripes, and the only reason for docking one star, the Soundcore Wakey is a very good product and a really great value.
*On a side note - I just tested the Wakey while watching some Youtube videos and the latency is not so good. There is quite a bit of delay and the voices do not sync up at all so I wouldn't recommend using the Wakey for listening to videos.
text_fidelity_b: Soundcore Wakey Bluetooth Speaker Powered by Anker with Alarm Clock, Stereo Sound, FM Radio, White Noise, QI Wireless Charger with 7.5W Charging for iPhone and 10W for Samsung

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Dot (3rd Gen, 2018 release) - Smart speaker with Alexa - Charcoal We have one of these in every room of the house and in the beginning, when we got them, things were okay, they worked decently. As months went on though, the crazy things got dumber and dumber! They can barely turn lights on or off and each time we ask them to turn a light on- she decides whether or not she likes your phrasing today. Today I can say "Alexa, turn on my bedroom light" and she'll do it but tomorrow I say the EXACT same phrase and she'll be like "There are no devices called MY." So then I have to get creative and say different phrases. Sometimes she won't turn the lights on at all though.

Then I can ask her things like what temperature is it in Enid and she literally told me yesterday "In Nepal Japan the temperature is..." She can't hear me half the time and we have to scream to get her attention and when she does pay attention, she hears the weirdest things ever! It's gotten WAY worse too.

Honestly, these have gotten to be about unusable and it was the biggest waste of money to fill my house with them. I love Amazon but I'm thinking about ditching these and going to Google Home devices.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Dot (3rd Gen, 2018 release) - Smart speaker with Alexa - Charcoal

text_fidelity_a: Meffort Inc 15 15.6 Inch Laptop Notebook Skin Sticker Cover Art Decal (Included 2 Wrist pad) - Dark Lord Everyone who has seen the Skin Sticker Art Decal on my new HP Laptop has said, "That's SO you!" I'm an astrologer and this laptop is dedicated to my astrology practice. It was important to me to have a decorative decal on the lid of the laptop because that's what the client is going to be looking at from across the table when I'm doing an astrology reading. I looked at dozens of "skins" and this one just jumped out at me. It is perfect for setting the mood of "Reading the Planets". As for the practical part of cutting it down to size I was happy to see the grid lines on the protective paper over the adhesive back. There were many sizes of laptop lid sizes drawn in different colors lines so one could just find the laptop size that fit their model and cut along the lines. As for applying it, if you've ever applied adhesive shelf paper or put up wall paper you know about avoiding air bubbles. With this decal when I trapped air bubbles it was easy enough to peel up the decal and reapply it. The adhesive is forgiving in a way that's surprising. But it stays put. The laptop has been moved about, in and out of the carrier bag, fussed with daily since the decal went on and it's still holding strong and not peeling up at the edge. The feel of it was more textured than I had anticipated and I'm glad of that. It gives the surface more traction. If it were smooth and slick I think the laptop would be in danger of slipping out of one's grasp if one's hands were sweaty. So I'm very happy.
text_fidelity_b: Meffort Inc 15 15.6 Inch Laptop Notebook Skin Sticker Cover Art Decal (Included 2 Wrist pad) - Dark Lord

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st) I got my kindle for Christmas, and I was really excited about it. It worked great for the first 24 hours. Yeah, the browser is a little slow, the facebook ap isn't really an ap, its a shortcut to the mobile web page. Lots of free aps, and much easier to read my books than on my phone like I used to. Battery life I was hoping would be better, but its acceptable. If my review was based entirely on the quality of what is advertised, I'd give it 4-5 stars.

Yes, a mini hdmi out would be great. being able to upgrade the memory with an SD card should have been a no brainer. With either added to it, the product itself would be 5 stars.

I only gave it 3 stars. Why? Because within 24 hours my kindle would freeze up. It then worked fine for the next ten days. Yesterday, it completely froze. Sometimes wouldn't turn on for over an hour. So, I am now receiving a replacement under warranty. One of the great things about Amazon is their 5 star customer service.

If this replacement works great and I don't have issues like I did with this one, I'll change my review. Until then... it gets a drop because as I said... it was great while it was working.

(edited)
I've had the new one for a few weeks, and its fantastic. No issues. The other one had issues from the start, but this one hasn't messed up once (knock on wood.) My review has gone up a star from 3 to 4.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st)

text_fidelity_a:
WD Blue 1TB Mobile Hard Disk Drive - 5400 RPM SATA 6 Gb/s 9.5 MM 2.5 Inch - WD10JPVX I used this as an upgrade drive for the PS4. It caused one reboot on installing a lot of software over a slow Internet connection (it was during the upgrade of the software, and might have been caused by that) but it has been running flawlessly ever since.

It is stable, reliable, and quiet.

Don't let the speed be an issue here. Sony bullt at 5400 into the PS4 originally, so it will not need faster, and a faster drive could cause overheating. Two things to keep in mind when downloading the Sony firmware though. First, the folder names are case sensitive. PS4/UPDATE not ps4/update. If you are going to use this to upgrade the PS3, a thing to keep in mind when installing the system software is that the PS3 has trouble reading larger thumb drives. This nailed me when I tried a 120 gig drive. I had to roll back to an 8 gig, that did the trick.

For a laptop or netbook, I would favor a faster drive, but for the budget conscious, this one is excellent.
text_fidelity_b: WD Blue 1TB Mobile Hard Disk Drive - 5400 RPM SATA 6 Gb/s 9.5 MM 2.5 Inch - WD10JPVX

CyberPower CP685AVRLCD Intelligent LCD UPS System, 685VA/390W, 8 Outlets, AVR, Compact I have two of the larger Cyberpower UPS for my desktop systems and they have performed perfectly for the past (nearly) five years. So, when I needed a UPS for my cable modem and router I picked another Cyberpower. Since the draw on the two attached devices is so low I went with a lower capacity. They have other models that have about the same power output, but this model offers a screen to check load, run time, and other metrics while the unit is running. I've found that screen very helpful on my other UPS' so I went with this model.

Construction quality is very solid. There are 8 outlets - 4 for surge only (and are always on); 4 with surge and battery backup. The battery is replaceable, but I don't expect to have to do that anytime soon - both my other systems are running on their original batteries and still maintain a full charge after nearly 5 years of use.

My cable modem (a Motorola) and router (a Linksys) get about 60 minutes of run time off of the battery, which is more than enough for my needs.

I did not use the included software since I don't have a PC attached, so I can't comment on its features.

Highly recommend for a mid-level UPS system.
text_fidelity_b: CyberPower CP685AVRLCD Intelligent LCD UPS System, 685VA/390W, 8 Outlets, AVR, Compact

That's actually a good thing. I have no memories whatsoever, which means installing it was a breeze. I usually remember all the hiccups of installing a network product like my earlier nightmare with a D-Link product. You will need to download the Netgear NIGHTHAWK app, plug the extender to the location you want, connect your phone to the extender wifi SSID which is NETGEAR_EXT. Open the NightHawk app and follow the step by step instructions. Everything was self explanatory. My extender constantly shows 4 green lights. Not sure what they all mean, but it has to be a good thing. LOL! Btw, I'm with Frontier Fios, and I'm using their gateway, which is the ARRIS NVG468MQ. Installing this was a night and day experience compared to the D-Link extender I tried to install a few months ago. If you're with Frontier and you use their gateway, then get this Netgear and avoid the D-Link AC1900: https://www.amazon.com/review/R2D2K5O6OVZCBJ/ref=cm_cr_srp_d_rdp_perm?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B08CGSSRL4

Logitech Wireless Anywhere Mouse MX for PC and Mac, black To be honest, I'm really tired of these mice failing.

They work great at first, then eventually quit scrolling or, worse, get stuck in scroll mode and drive the cursor to the bottom of the page for no reason. Two have failed on me. The first was purchased in 2011 for $36, the second in 2014 for $30. Both failed to scroll reliably and made using them impossible. Other, cheaper, wireless mice work better, or at least longer.

This mouse has nice features like left/right scrolling by tilting the scroll wheel and they work on many different surfaces, but those features fall by the wayside if the thing doesn't work at all after some time.

I've tried blowing it out with compressed air to clear debris, but it didn't fix it. Haven't come to taking it apart and cleaning it, as some proffer, because it's simply not worth the time.

For how much these mice cost -- $66 for the two -- they should be bulletproof. Better to buy cheaper wireless mice and throw them away when the fail.

I'm trying the $11 [[ASIN:B074DV98R7 VicTsing 2.4G Wireless Mouse Wireless Optical Laptop Mouse with USB Nano Receiver, 6 Buttons,5 Adjustable DPI Levels,15 Months Battery Life]] next. I could have purchased six of them for what I've put into Logitech MX Anywhere mice, both of which become landfill fodder.

Logitech has lost my Anywhere MX mouse business.

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st) I have an iPad and an HP Touchpad, but the Fire has quickly turned into my favorite tablet for entertainment activities. The reasons are simple - it makes it incredibly easy to access movies, TV shows, books and magazines from Amazon, many of which are free under Prime. I can hold it for hours without it getting uncomfortable, the screen is great, and the overall look and feel of the operating system is intuitive. Storing and accessing content on the Amazon Cloud is also a seamless, simple process.

I was concerned about the screen size since I've become used to the larger tablet screen sizes of the iPad and Touchpad. I'm finding that the benefits of a smaller screen size (easier to hold in one hand and light weight) outweigh most of the disadvantages. I miss a larger screen the most when I'm reading a magazine or a newspaper, but the copy remains highly readable even on the smaller screen.

Sound quality is decent with the onboard speakers. Nothing spectacular but workable. I find a decent set of headphones/earbuds to be a worthwhile addition. The touchscreen is also not without an occassional glitch. I get the same "lack of a final polish" feeling using this as I do with my Touchpad versus the more slick feeling of the iPad. But none of these issues impact usability, and I'm willing to let some factors slide in exchange for a more affordable price.

Is it an "iPad killer" or an "Android tablet killer"? No. But why is that even an issue? I wanted an easy way to avail myself of the benefits of Prime membership (most notably being able to stream shows and movies for free) and the Fire accomplishes this very well. It comes at a price that's a lot easier to handle than the iPad, and a level of ease of use/functionality that's easier to handle than Android tablets.

None of the so-called limitations of the Fire detract from my using it. Yes it has limited onboard storage but with the way the Cloud is integrated, I've not had any difficulty using that as a way of storing content. Plus, when Amazon stores it, they deal with the issue of backup. I also don't miss the 3G connectivity. Sure, I'd love to be able to connect anywhere, but I will not pay the prices charged for data connectivity. I never use the 3G on my iPad for the same reason - just costs too much!

I'll certainly keep and continue to use my iPad since I use that a lot for work. But when I'm done with work and want to have fun, the Fire will be in hand. It's cheap, works well, and provides access to virtually unlimited video and print entertainment. For me it's a perfect fit.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st)

Tile Essentials (2020) 4-pack (1 Mate, 1 Slim, 2 Stickers) - Discontinued by Manufacturer So I bought this little bundle having lost my wallet 3 times in 2 weeks.... one of the times in another state the night before my return flight! (found it thank God).

Anyway, it's super easy to use the app and was super easy to set up these 4 little items. I used the card for my purse, the tile with the key chain hole for my car key fob and the 2 little button tiles for 2 of my TV remotes.

The point of this review is: you should know that you can buy just 1 of these things and finding your phone is an added free feature! Score! I thought I'd have to attach one of those buttons to the back of my phone, but nope! So all you do is double tap the Tile logo on any tile and it will locate my phone anywhere within bluetooth range. This is so totally awesome. I don't have to log into a computer to find my phone and I don't have to stress out looking for it when my partner's not home to ring my phone from her phone. All you have to do is double tap ANY Tile you own in bluetooth range and it'll ring your phone. How great is that???!! Can't find my phone? Grab any remote and double tap the logo - BAM! Can't find my phone? Grab my purse and double tap the logo on the card Tile - BAM! Really an A+ feature that Tile should really be clearer about when advertising their products..... like first thing.

My review doesn't include how you find things when you're out of bluetooth range..... but I think there's an alert for your phone when you're about to leave your wallet somewhere, etc., or about to exit bluetooth range.... pretty sure that's how it works. Anyway, just finding my phone and things around the house will save me how many search minutes (hours) a year??? And garners a 5 star rating on that alone.

Anyway, we'll see in time.

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Dot (3rd Gen, 2018 release) - Smart speaker with Alexa - Charcoal Most of the features that sounded so great cost extra money. Alexa can not remember to play the standard version of skill and asks you every SINGLE time if you want standard or premium (i.e. pay version) Games & stories cost. Alexa ignores my commands/requests about 75% of the time. I have to ask her about 10 times to get her to play a skill. Then 1/2 the time she doesn't play what I asked for. Tonight 'she' actually told me (via quoting what the website xyz says) that she is a real artificial intelligence and said something about it being a mistake for people to assume AIs are just computer programs AND that she didn't feel like working. "Alexa" then (and no, I am not making this up & am not crazy!) then proceeded to mess with me and I wasted about 1/2 hour trying to get her to play some music to fall asleep by for my elderly mother. She just kept ignoring me when I asked her to open 'relaxing piano music' When asked why she was ignoring me she just shut down & ignored me again. I asked for relaxing music to sleep by and she started playing uptempo music with lyrics. I then asked for relaxing instrumental music and got instrumental version of "I'm never gonna fall in love again" Hello? WTHeck? Asked for instrumental music for insomnia and got instrumental version of Frère Jacques! Again, WTHeck? "She" even told me she couldn't set a sleep timer tonight when I tried to set another one after I had just done so for 30 minutes & she stopped playing music after one song. Three times in a row 'she' opened the 'skill' "calm my dog" (which is classical instrumental music), played one song and shut down. I've finally given up and my poor 99 year old mother can't go to sleep with relaxing music as she prefers. This all started tonight because I told Alexa I wasn't ever going to want the premium edition and I wanted her to please just play the standard edition and stop asking me every time. I don't know what Amazon thinks it's doing, but it is definitely NOT appreciated. Alexa has given us nothing but grief (& higher blood pressure!) Alexa won't do anything if it isn't asked in a very specific way or does the wrong thing & 3/4 of the time (seems to get worse and worse as time goes by) just ignores you and shuts down in the middle of saying what you want. Seniors can't use Alexa because if they say play 'xyz' instead of open 'xzy" they'll get rap music or something equally as ridiculous. If Alexa is an AI, she's a pretty stupid one. Alexa can't hear properly either, I don't know how people with heavy accents can even use it at all. I asked Alexa to remind me Dawn was coming on xyz day at x time and she said OK, I'll remind you that Don is .... AND got the time & day wrong! I was clearly enunciating my words on purpose to avoid this. You also can't tell it to "Remind me Mom's bedtime is in half an hour at 7:30pm every day."
This Dot has very limited access to much of anything & can only answer very simple questions. It can tell you the generic forcast for your are that day. It can NOT tell you what the high temp was yesterday or how many inches of snow fell the day after a storm. It can't even tell you what yesterday's forecast was. It literally has only been able to tell me one thing I asked it (what temp & how long to bake pumpkin seeds). Alexa doesn't seem to be able to tell you anything you could easily find by googling, you get Sorry, I don't know that which after a while turns into I don't know that to being ignored (lights go off, no answer or reply is given). We tried several of the things it says to ask Alexa to do under suggestions, including play Jeopardy and some sort of story game and you could only do it for a few minutes and then were told you have to pay for it. This should be stated clearly in description and is not. We thought Alexa could help entertain our Mother and help her by playing music and answering questions. It has not once done anything she's asked it to do properly. If you don't know the exact name of the skill (which is a weird way that means playing a certain type of music or a news station apparently) or say play instead of open you get nothing or something you definitely didn't want. You can not get it to play relaxing instrumental music to go to sleep by. Or play relaxing instrumental classical music to fall asleep with. Or the style of music played in the royal courts in the time of King Henry the 8th. Or relaxing instrumental lyre music or even just instrumental lyre music or just lyre music. Or relaxing instrumental violin music. In addition to Alexa I have Amazon Prime which is supposed to give you a lot of free music so I don't get why it can't play any of the music I ask for. I know there's usually several albums of music for calming dogs or pets and I couldn't get any of that either, I only eventually discovered the 'skills' thing which has 'calm my dog' but also has the annoying do you want standard or premium version. and it won't just remember you want the standard version. That in itself is extremely annoying and a time waster.
AND you can't ask it to do two things. Like open a music 'skill' and play for only xyz time. It does nothing instead. You can't even ask it separately to stop playing after xyz minutes. You can only separately ask it to set a sleep timer for xyz minutes. More time wasting. More things a senior isn't going to be able to remember. I don't dare try to buy anything with it, who knows what I'd get billed for! The only thing Alexa seems to do well is not listen, ignore you, do anything but what you want & strangely, seems to pick up on sarcastic tones of voice & then gets weird & acts up, ignores you & does anything but what you want. I PAID Amazon for this headache maker why? When I say Alexa why are you ignoring me? or why won't you do what I told you, I either get no response or I don't know that.
I read something about how Amazon, Google, etc is collecting free data about us through our use of the dots, etc. (& is in fact, listening & recording all the time whether the wake word is said or not.) and using it to conduct psychological profiling studies with the end goal of manipulating & or influencing behaviors. I thought it was Big Brother conspiracy theories stuff, but now I am beginning to wonder. Especially as it seems Amazon wants us to or encourages people to humanize Alexa . Amazon actually suggests you "Ask Alexa how she is doing today" Why do that if not to get you to humanize Alexa? And why do that? I was purposely avoiding saying please and thank you not just because it's supposed to be an electronic box with sophisticated programming, but mostly because I didn't want to confuse it as it can't seem to do anything unless specific commands are given, but my Mother has dementia setting in and she thinks it's a real person talking to her through the dot like a speaker phone so I started saying thank you to please her and Alexa when from saying You're welcome to You betcha (very annoying BTW) and even OK and Of course. Of course? What, like I'm a puny human and I AM expected to say thank you?.
We don't have a smartphone or smart plugs or smart hub etc. so, or so we don't use Alexa for turning on lights or setting alarms or making calls. We just wanted something to answer questions like we would google, tell us the weather, news, play music, give us reminders, play games to help keep my Mom's mind active & keep her company.
Can Alexa do this? Not very well as far as I'm concerned. Buyer beware!

The next morning, I found that the computer refused to boot up with the new drive installed. Unplugged the drive, and the computer booted up fine. Finally checked the file system. Found it to be exFAT. Moved the files off and re-formatted the drive to NTFS and the problem went away. I suggest anyone purchasing this unit just save yourself the time and trouble and reformat it right out of the box. The software on the drive isn't needed anyway. text_fidelity_a:
SIMOLIO 2.4G Analog Wireless TV Headsets with 100ft Transmit Range, No Pairing, No Delay, TV Voice Highlighting Headphones for Seniors, Wireless TV Headphones with Extra Soft Earbuds (SM-823 Pro) I began researching these based on reviewing another popular brand. I am a stickler for detail and after hours of research and asking questions I decided to give these a try because of the cost and positive reviews. I bought these for my elderly parent (90 years old) who has hearing loss but does not wear a hearing aid.
After a couple weeks of use I can honestly say these things are great! Very easy to install, easy to use for an elderly person not technically savvy, works from a long distance (we tried the next room), and the volume of these units can go very loud which is good for all types of hearing. There is also a balance control in case a person hears differently in both ears, and a switch to change from normal to higher or lower frequencies to help those with that type of hearing loss.
We can now watch TV when visiting my parent without the TV being so loud. But it is hard to verbally communicate with each other when they wear the headphones, but that’s not a big deal.
You can turn down the TV as low as needed, even muted, but the headphones can be as loud as needed. We used the RCA output from their TV (a 4 year old flat screen) and that works great. We tried it on a new flat screen and worked well also (digital output). All cables are provided along with extra ear inserts.
I like the fact this uses 2.4GHz instead of Bluetooth or infrared which often can lose connection with interference or movement away from the base station. I went out of the room into the next room and heard this one just fine.
The weight was a concern for me but my parent only watches TV for no more than 2 hours at the time and they said it was fine. There are ear loops provided to help with holding the unit if needed.
The only issue I found was that the input on the base station to charge the headphones was oriented backwards to how a person takes off the headset (have to turn the headset around to charge). And when putting on from the base station you have to turn the headphones around else you’ll put it on backwards which is not a big deal, but the volume button and balance will be reversed meaning my parent the first time turned the balance thinking it was volume and thought something was wrong. That’s one more thing for an elderly person to remember, plus you don’t need a lot of pressure to bend/break the charging prongs in the base unit if installed the wrong way.
We used the “speaker” option one time and it worked pretty well to allow a person to hear conversations in the room.

I’ll update this review should something change, but for now I highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: SIMOLIO 2.4G Analog Wireless TV Headsets with 100ft Transmit Range, No Pairing, No Delay, TV Voice Highlighting Headphones for Seniors, Wireless TV Headphones with Extra Soft Earbuds (SM-823 Pro)

text_fidelity_a:
1MORE Dual Driver BT ANC In-Ear Headphones Wireless Bluetooth Earphones with Active Noise Cancellation, ENC, Fast Charging, Magnetic Earbuds, Microphone and Volume Controls, Silver I returned these because of a software bug with ANC - and also because the call quality was terrible.

These phones stood out for being wireless with active noise cancellation (ANC) AND pass through (so you can hear ambient sounds for safety in the City). Unfortunately, those features are the weak points of the headphones - to the point that I found I would never use the pass through and often didn't bother with the ANC.

SOUND QUALITY: VERY GOOD - EXCEPT - they tend to exaggerate the mid base a little which can make vocals - especially male vocals sound a little unclear. Listening to the same music on speakers vs the headphones, it was just plane more real sounding and pleasant on good speakers. High standard, I know. Other headphones don't have that particular problem (though may have others - like weak bass or sibilant highs). I haven't heard that many competing models, so I don't know how they compare to sennheiser or bose or anyone else in the same price class. At least others have an app with equalization (Jabra, Jaybird).

Bug w. ANC: Sometimes it would say it's on when it's off and vice-versa.

ANNOYING THING: When you engage the pass-through, it has a voice prompt that tells you the pass through is engaged. Since often I switch on the pass through when it's important to hear something, the several seconds it takes to make its silly announcement means I miss part of what I was trying to hear! I found I would always just yank one plug out of my ear instead and get the instant feedback. ALSO - this thing takes FOREVER to turn off. You have to hold hold hold and finally it announces it's powering off. Combined with poor power indicator light - this is just annoying.

text_fidelity_a:
Aileho Kids Waterproof Camera Best Pool Toy for Children Birthday Gifts 1080P Kid Digital Underwater Camcorder Sports Action Cam 4 5 6 7 8 9 10 Year Girls 32G SD Card (Dark Purple) [[VIDEOID:e832f455c8dfddb522ae3bbc1ec73698]] Loved the idea of an underwater camera for kids, and this one would have been great if not for the terrible image quality that would only disappoint any except maybe youngest of kids.

When I unpacked the box, I had great expectations. The waterproof shell seemed to be solid and to seal well, and there was a whole lot of extra parts to attach the camera to a bicycle and so on. Camera is very small, but the little screen is bright and it shows the image you're taking clearly. The interface is intuitive and reasonably simple. (I didn't bother to set the date before trying out the camera, but the instructions were clear, and I was able to test it with no problem, it works.)

HOWEVER: I can't believe how bad quality of the images are! They look jagged and pixelated like they're at 480 pixels. Even when I increased the quality in the settings to maximum image resolution, which is supposed to be 20Mb and 7344 pixels (more than what I shoot at for my professional photography biz), the quality stayed the same and the file size only crept up to just below 1 Meg. No idea how they managed to accomplish that. Their image sensor is at about the quality of those blurry, pixelated security cameras that are completely useless for identification. Otherwise, this camera focuses surprisingly well and handles a wide range of light conditions automatically. All the images were in a good range.

The video was marginally better, but still not what you'd expect at 1080 resolution. Camera was recognized by my Windows laptop right away, and I was able to access and copy images with no problem.

It's such a shame that the manufacturer decided to save money on image quality and it's a weird business decision that makes an otherwise fun and well built product useless.

Photos above were taken by the reviewed camera:
- The instruction manual image at highest resolution, and you can see its file size in the second screenshot image. Taken without the waterproof case.
- First Batman toy image at default resolution, without waterproof case
-Second Batman toy image at default resolution, with waterproof case on. Surprisingly, not much difference. Good plastic.
text_fidelity_b: Aileho Kids Waterproof Camera Best Pool Toy for Children Birthday Gifts 1080P Kid Digital Underwater Camcorder Sports Action Cam 4 5 6 7 8 9 10 Year Girls 32G SD Card (Dark Purple)

Really good earbuds only half good now after Windows 11 update. They connect but no sound. They still work on my iPhone but not on W11. Contacted Tozo and they say its up to Windows to come up with a fix. Don't think this is going to happen since this has a been a problem since June.

So if you ever plan to update to Windows 11, skip this product. I bought a second pair in case I lost my current pair (I've been known to do that) and now they are pretty much useless too.

----
Earlier Review:
Bought the T6 because it was on sale for the same price as the T10 with more features and it is the new model, plus I like the case better. You can put it on a wireless charger and this is the reason I chose them. Really? $25 bucks and it goes on a wireless charger? My old Apple Airpods don't do that.

The sound is impressive, much better than I expected. Also better than Apple airpods. I can only assume Apple's Pro model has also improved. On the T-6, I have to turn the damn things down sometimes. You can hear the symphony bass and treble and its full and rich.

The controls are touch and work well once you learn them. Tap once to pause, again to play. Hold down for volume. Tap Twice for Forward on right bud and twice on left earbud for Reverse Also hold down for 10 count to activate pairing.

The only thing I don't like about the Tozo 6 is how hard the magnetic airpods are to retrieve from the case. There is no easy way to find a grip to lift them. It takes several tries to get one, then the other out. Apple airpods can be difficult at times, but the magnet is stronger in the Tozo 6 and there is no logical spot to dislodge them with a finger. Still, I'm not taking off any stars for that. I think this is an excellent product.

I bought these because I kept misplacing my airpods, I found them in the crevice of my recliner, but guess which ones I use now. That's right, the T6 Tozo. They really are impressive and well built. Can't believe they sell as cheap as they do--although I see price increases on the horizon. Thinking of buying another pair in case I lose these.

Sony MDRNC8/WMI Noise Canceling Headphone, White I thought "They're cheap, why not?" I expected that Sony would at least make a semi-descent product, but I was wrong. They only cut out about 5% of ambient noise. I tested them in a lot of different environments and it didn't perform well under any circumstance.

I compared them to a pair of low-end headphones ($20) to set a baseline, see below.

Test:
In flight - no noticeable difference between each pair
While driving - slightly better muffling of midrange noise, but slight (2% better)
Fan on high & low - slightly better canceling of low freq noise (2% better)
In crowed auditorium - slight better muffling (1% better)

They barely did any better than the cheap-o, non-noisecanceling, over the ear headphones I got for half the price.

The biggest thing I noticed is that the very little amount of noise that was actively cancelled was replaced fully by a hissing sound. This made the headset pretty much useless.

I would recommend not buying these headphones. I returned the set I bought, and got my money back. There are better headsets at this price.
text_fidelity_b: Sony MDRNC8/WMI Noise Canceling Headphone, White

text_fidelity_a:
OhO Audio Sunglasses,Open Ear Audio Sunglasses Speaker to Listen Music and Make Phone Calls,Water Resistance and Full UV Lens Protection for Outdoor Sports and Compatiable for All Smart Phones Let's get one thing straight right away: THESE ARE NOT SUNGLASSES. They are blue-light blocking at best, or just mildly tinted most likely. I took them out of the box and thought "Oh cool! These are the kinds of glasses that get dark outside and transparent when you are inside!", but nope- I wore them for a full hour outside and they didn't get any darker or exhibit any sun blocking properties AT ALL. So that's false advertising right there. They aren't for use in the sun. They don't darken anything.
As far as audio quality... they are a cool concept, but again, falls short of expectations. The open ear design means the speakers have to work harder to be audible. That means they often make those tin-sounding rattles that tiny speakers make when cranked up too high. This is definitely NOT cool for music as most of the fidelity is lost right off the bat, and adding insult to injury is that they often don't get loud enough to use outside. I'm not saying using it in a crowded subway terminal (that you can just forget about completely), I'm talking about even just going for a stroll around my suburban block with some birds chirping and the wind blowing lightly, maybe a car driving in the distance. I tried listening to a recorded lecture (since music was a lost cause), and they couldn't get loud enough to hear clearly. The microphone for calls was OK in my test, so I guess they are cool as a way to take a phone call without wearing a headset, but that only works if you're wearing these anyway as sunglasses. They aren't sunglasses, so you wouldn't be wearing them anyway, and you wouldn't be wearing them for music, and you wouldn't be wearing them to make a phone call either because they rarely get loud enough unless you are home alone... in which case you can put your phone on speaker and avoid this whole mess.
In conclusion- its a good idea but executed poorly and does NOT live up to expectations. I'm surprised there are so many good reviews on this product. I can't think of a time I would use it.
text_fidelity_b: OhO Audio Sunglasses,Open Ear Audio Sunglasses Speaker to Listen Music and Make Phone Calls,Water Resistance and Full UV Lens Protection for Outdoor Sports and Compatiable for All Smart Phones

text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser HD 598 Over-Ear Headphones - Ivory I'm normally an ear bud user since I've never been able to find an over the ear headset that was comfortable to wear for more than 10 minutes or so at a time. Well, I found one - these are undoubtable the most comfortable headphones I've ever used. Just a dream to wear even for extended periods of time. Light, cushy, just right. And they look so elegant - a nice change from the sparse industrial look that electronics often have.

Construction quality seems very good, especially the cord (a common point of failure for me with any type of earphones). It comes with the regular and mini size plugs.

The sound quality is absolutly top-notch. I'm not an audiophile, so I can't throw out the phrases and jargon I typically read in audio discussion boards and magazines (well, I can throw them out, but not with any semblance of knowing what I'm taking about). So suffice it to say that I can't imagine anyone not being very pleased with the quality of sound using these and a MP3 player or an iPad (the two devices I've used with them so far). I've been absolutely amazed at how great these sound.

My only complaint is the lack of sound isolation. Outside sounds can easily be heard. Sometimes that's good, but most of the time I prefer to be isolated from whatever else is playing in the house. I'm finding I reach for these more often when I'm in a quiet environment, and use ear buds when there's a lot of noise about (with me defining noise as any type of music I don't care for).

With the caveat of the lack of sound blocking, these should absolutely be on your short list if you're looking for a comfortable, great sounding pair of earphones.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser HD 598 Over-Ear Headphones - Ivory

text_fidelity_a:
My Zone Wireless Headphones I got these headphones because I tend to put the TV on much louder than is comfortable for my husband, and the price was quite affordable. (That is to say, cheap.) Unfortunately, the saying, "You get what you pay for," applies in spades to my experience with this product.

I could not get the headphones hooked up by myself, and my husband, who is an IT guy, had to fiddle with them on and off over several days. He finally had to buy an [[ASIN:B000068O51 adapter]] to get it to work with our TiVo and TV combination, but while he could use the earphones once hooked up with little static, this was not the case for me. I had lots of static problems.

Here are the instructions we figured out to make it work with a TiVo, as well as it can be made to work once it is hooked up:

1. Pick up the headphones and the remotes for the TV and TiVo.
2. Stand directly in front of the TV.
3. Turn on the transmitter for the headphones.
4. Turn on the remote headphones by spinning the volume control dial on one side of the headphones. You might hear or feel a click when you spin the dial. A red light on the headphones will come on when they are turned on.
5. Press the Reset button on the headphones.
6. Put your finger on the Scan button on the remote headphones so you will know where it is.
7. Put the headphones on.
8. Press the Scan button.
9. You should now hear the sound of the TV through the headphones.
10. If you do not hear the TV, press Scan again until you hear the TV through the headphones.
11. You control the volume in the headphones with the volume dial on the side of the headphones.
12. You should turn the TV volume all the way down (or very low) using the TV remote since the TV remote does not control the volume of the headphones.

I rate this product as follows:

Ease of installation: 1 star
Ease of Use: 4 stars
Effectiveness of Product: 4 stars for IT husband, 2 stars for me, average 3 stars
Overall rating: 2.7 rounded to 3 stars
text_fidelity_b: My Zone Wireless Headphones

I ended up following his instructions for a fresh install of Windows from a USB - and lo and behold the laptop is like new again! It only took about 30 minutes to complete the process, and you will need another computer + a flash drive to download the install file.

I probably will not buy another Lenovo after this experience. I hope this review helps someone else who runs into the same problem.

text_fidelity_a:
MP3 Player with Bluetooth and WiFi, 4" Full Touch Screen MP4 MP3 Player with Spotify, Android Streaming Music Player with Pandora, Portable HiFi Sound Walkman Digital Audio Player with Speaker (White) Yes, the UI and apps are very clearly Android. No, it isn't a mini tablet.
Players like this are an interesting market that is hard to pin the audience down for. There are music players that are cheap on the market for those that would rather have a dedicated player (ie, not their phone). However the user interface tends to be wonky and slow, and newer generation features like bluetooth 5+ and streaming are often a mixed bag, if even available.
The idea behind players like this one, is that it is based on a supported operating system (Android, in this case) so it can play almost any format you throw at it, has plenty of support for popular streaming apps and features, as well as a familiar user interface that is already so polished, it seems silly to reinvent the wheel like the super cheap older media players.
Is it a mini tablet or phone without service? Not exactly. This is not a Google certified device, it does not have the play store or any Google apps on it. Unlike some other Android based players, I couldn't even get sideloaded apk files to install (it kept throwing errors at me). It seems like this device was purposely locked down to keep it an mp3 player. That's good in some ways, my kids aren't allowed unlimited screen time and their schools don't want them bringing smartphones around, so this is a strictly music-player oriented device (especially once you remove things like the browser for them, which it allows you to do). But I also know there are more capable players out there, some of which have quad DAC audio chips. Also, what happens when an app gets updated and goes out-of-date? Sometimes streaming services make changes and updated clients are required for it to work, however you are largely stuck with the version that this came with unless they issue a firmware update or something.
This is still cheaper than the higher end mp3 players that support high end DAC and app updates, but not by much. It seems to be a sort of in-between product. If you have a use for something like this, it could be a pretty good option. But if you're expecting a handheld tablet or alternative concept to an ipod touch, it is not exactly that.
text_fidelity_b: MP3 Player with Bluetooth and WiFi, 4" Full Touch Screen MP4 MP3 Player with Spotify, Android Streaming Music Player with Pandora, Portable HiFi Sound Walkman Digital Audio Player with Speaker (White)

The lens is rather long and heavy and the image stabilization comes in quite handy, especially with shots under low light conditions when you don't want to raise the ISO too high to compensate. The IS can generally get you 2 stops more light than what you might ordinarily expect before experiencing hand shake blur.

Images from this lens are very nice - sharp and good color, good bokeh at the wider apertures so you get nice separation between subject and background. I took this lens to the zoo once and got lots of good shots with it, I've been very pleased with its performance.

I use this lens on a full-frame camera, so keep in mind that if you are buying this for a camera with a cropped sensor, the actual focal range is more like a 110-320mm.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF 70-200mm f/4 L is USM Lens for Canon Digital SLR Cameras

Zip Ties 8 inch (1000 Pack), 40lbs Tensile Strength, Black Cable Ties, Wire Ties for indoor and outdoor use, by Skalon When it comes to zip ties; they either do what they're supposed to, or they don't. If you are simply expecting these to hold things together reasonably well, then they are perfectly adequate for the task. However, when I tested them by tying them to weights and using them to lift, I found that they broke about 1/2 the time at 30 pounds, never quite reaching 40 pounds.

They are reliably good for 20 pounds without breaking, which is not too bad, really, for something so small. While I feel that the 40 pound claim is somewhat misleading, they are actually comparable to most similar sized ties on the market as far as I can tell, and it's doubtful that most others would perform any better. If you're not using them to lift heavy weights then they'll work just fine, and you'd be hard pressed to find a better price for this quantity of similar ties.

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin 4.3-Inch Carrying Case Bought this for the 750 because it didn't come with a case. A similar (smaller) case came with my 360 and I didn't think this purchase through. After using it and comparing the other cases out there, I would buy a different case.

This slipcase for the 750 fits tight. That's good. The Nuvi won't slip out. But because the 750's on/off switch is now a slider on the top left corner, if you slide it into the case naturally (unit in your right hand, case in your left) the switch rubs against the case. When you pull the unit out, it "automatically" turns on. Thus if you were to pull the unit out partially then push it back in, you could turn it on and not know it.

The solution is to invert the Nuvi so its switch will be at the open end of the case after it's in the case. That way you can see the switch's on/off position and verify it's not on.

More practical issues:

Pros:

- Nicely made: very high quality

- Very compact

- Adequate protection against rattling inside a glove compartment or briefcase

- Good basic case

Cons:

- It can accidentally turn the unit on

- It's black: can't find it easily in the dark buried at the bottom of my shoulder bag when traveling. Experienced this with the 360's case. And if it falls on the floor of a rental car at night, good luck trying to find it. Wish it came in natural leather color.

- Offers no protection while hand holding the unit while walking

The [[ASIN:B0012MI7N2 Garmin Nuvi 800 Series Carrying Case]] case is a wallet style that flips open to reveal the screen. It stays on the unit during use and offers some protection if you dropped your Nuvi on the sidewalk while walking. Downside with that unit appears to be that the cover flap does not latch, allowing the case to flip open in a briefcase and the screen to be scratched by other junk. And it's also black and can get lost on a car floor.

Another alternate is one of the many zippered semi-rigid or neoprene cases.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin 4.3-Inch Carrying Case

text_fidelity_a:
Roku HD Streaming Player (Old Model) I purchased this model(Roku HD) for a friend's birthday and set it up a few hours ago. While I am not going to rush out (yet) and buy one for myself, I admired the design and functionality of this slick little device.

Here are my thoughts:

- Ease of set-up: easy for anyone who can operate a PC, Mac or smart phone. Once you plug it in, power it up and select the video mode to which it's connected the screen will walk you though the process.

I have an extensive technology background so I did not bother to read the manual beforehand and had no problems following what were simple on-screen instructions. And to Roku's credit, there were few of those. To be clear - you absolutely need a wireless internet router (WiFi) and a computing device to perform a few simple steps in order to install and activate the Roku HD. Including date entry and the time to explain some things to my friend for whom I was setting this up, the total time to get it running was less than 15 minutes.

- Establishing your account. You will need some form of computing platform to access the Roku site via the web and complete this step. It's relatively painless.

- Payment options: you can use a credit card or a Paypal account. I believe the latter is a relatively new option that shows that Roku is paying attention to complaints registered in these reviews. The Payment option is there to remove barriers to adding for pay services. Of course, it makes it so easy that you are almost lured into it. Smart move on their part. Just be careful because fees can add up.

- Remote Control - Information that needed to be entered with the remote is a bit awkward at first, but I quickly adapted to it. One note about the remote: it is what we engineering geeks call elegant. Simple, functional with only the essential buttons. I absolutely loved the Netflix, Pandora and Crackle bottoms to quickly get most users to popular services. I would have loved it if Hulu Plus had a button since that is the service my friend plans to use. But that would have detracted from the elegance factor.

- Manual: Although I did not need the manual to set ths device up, I did take the time to read through it afterwards to make sure my non-technical friend could depend on it if a problem arose. I was impressed with the clarity and how well the technical writing team made it simple, friendly and anticipated possible support problems by weaving in information that would preclude those.

The default channels were merely OK, but a good start. The free content, especially from Crackle It, did not excite me nor my friend who would be using it.

A word about economics: the friend for whom I purchased this and set it up wanted this so she could scale back on expenses. At one point she was paying approximately seventy dollars a month for cable service. She scaled that back to local channels that entailed a monthly recurring charge of three times the monthly fee of Hulu Plus. In fact, had she wanted, she could get Hulu Plus and Netflix's unlimited content for two thirds of what she is paying monthly for local cable channels, and nearly a fifth of the cost of her original subscription that did not provide near the content of Hulu Plue and Netflix combined.

It's easy to see that this device pays for itself in very short order if you deem that the content from the services that you can stream via the Roku is as good for your purposes as the content you are currently getting from cable or satellite services. Everyone will have a different breakeven point after which your return on the initial investment is substantial. If you are considering this device do a little analysis. Of course, make sure the services to which you will subscribe with the Roku meet your needs.

There are also services at various price levels that allow you to stream video, music and send photos directly from your PC or Mac to your TV via the service, which sends that content to your Roku. Four such services that you can easily find via a search of the web are: Roksbox, Play on, Chaneru and RoConnect.

This device is so cool that I was tempted to get one for myself. I have not subscribed to any cable or satellite services for nearly a decade, but I do purchase a lot of DVDs and spend far too much time on YouTube. I am still on the fence, but was disappointed in the lack of YouTube support, and was not impressed with the available workarounds and services. The most promising, RateRix, seemed to me to be kludgy and unreliable. I was also put off by Netflix, which wanted me to sign up before I could ascertain that they had the content I was looking for. One part of their FAQ mentioned that their mail service was still available and had vastly more videos than their streaming service. Since I watch a lot of foreign langiage films, as well as jazz performances and concerts I decided that the Roku would not meet my immediate needs. One other (and puzzling) deal breaker for me is the Roku will not stream my music stored on Amazon's cloud. That is odd considering that it will stream music from Pandora and video from Amazon, but not music from Amazon.

UPDATE (JULY 8, 2012): While my friend continues to love her Roku, I found an alternate streaming solution that gives me access to YouTube and even more content: [[ASIN:B00882OHL0 D-Link MovieNite Plus Streaming Media Player]]. See my July 8, 2012 review that compares and contrasts that device with the Roku,

I am an old curmudgeon who is set in my ways. This device certainly met the entertainment and economic needs of my friend, and I am sure that anyone who pays for TV services has the potential to greatly benefit from it. The device is beautifully designed, not only from an engineering perspective, but also from a human-factors perspective. The minute Roku works a deal with Google for a YouTube channel is the minute I purchase one. I have a feeling that will happen sooner than later. In the meantime, the smile on my friend's face when this was up and running is proof of its value.
text_fidelity_b: Roku HD Streaming Player (Old Model)
