iHome Smart Brief: 13 inch Laptop Briefcase for Mac, Heathered Grey Last year I switched to a Macbook Pro 13-inch after being a PC user since the early eighties. I love my Mac, but I haven't gone whole-hog for the rest of the pricey iProducts Apple puts out. Still, this case is just about perfect for my needs.

First, I like how the zippered compartment for the computer does not unzip all around. It's really easy to slip my Mac in and out of its fleecy padded pocket while still feeling like it's protected. (There's also plenty of room for my little wireless mouse dongle, although I don't use a mouse much anymore.) The iPad compartment is similar, and it holds my Kindle Fire in its rooCase with room to spare for something else (like a checkbook or wallet perhaps). The clever half-case compartment with pockets for chargers, headphones, and pens has plenty of room for my Mac power supply, Kindle charger and cables, and another charger if I need it.

The full compartment in the middle of the case is for whatever you might stick in it. It's not huge in depth, but it would certainly hold a legal pad/portfolio and a magazine or two. I don't use a cell phone now, but one day I might, so the outer pocket for the phone is nice; it's also serviceable for one of those small flashlights or perhaps a set of keys (on the right keychain). Toothbrush! I could see using the sleeve as a lapdesk/laptop stand while seated on a plane or in a doctor's office.

The sleeve comes with a classy, comfortable shoulder strap with strong, reliable clips. At first it wasn't clear what the the clips were supposed to clip to, but they are hidden away under the edges of the center gusset (what you see as the narrow black line running across the thickness in the photo here). There's no tangling up with this shoulder strap, either; the business ends can be rotated to keep the strap straight.

It's lightweight. And the color? It's a perfect match for the Mac Lion startup screen, of course. Everything about it says "Mac," including the iHome logo, but you don't have to be an Apple nut to love this sleeve. Very well designed.
text_fidelity_b: iHome Smart Brief: 13 inch Laptop Briefcase for Mac, Heathered Grey

While my TV would allow me to connect to the sound bar via Bluetooth I opted to connect via the HDMI ARC connection to avoid any sound lag. In addition to these 2 connection options you can connect via the included optical cable.

I followed the instructions - plugged the HDMI cable (not included) into the ARC HDMI port, plugged the sound bar and subwoofer into the surge protector and turned everything on. The TV automatically recognized the soundbar and changed my output.

All I had to do was press the “secure link” button on the remote and the sound bar wirelessly linked to the subwoofer without issue.

I decided to move the subwoofer to another area of the room - I unplugged it, moved it, plugged it back in and it reconnected without any problem.

I was able to pair the system with my iPhone without any issue and the sound is stunning. From the rich bass of the subwoofer, the vibrant midtones, to the crisp highs - every note is clear and distinct.

While I have a true 5.1 surround system most of the TV broadcasts are not going to utilize that type of system and the sound is actually richer through a sound bar with a subwoofer.

This soundbar can be easily wall mounted using the included template.

The entire system is intuitive and user friendly. While many sound systems require hours to hook up and figure out how to use correctly this one is so straightforward. The remote doesn’t have a bunch of excess buttons that you’ll never need or use.

In my instance my TV remote was able to control it immediately with no issues.

I highly recommend this soundbar for anyone looking for an easy way to improve the quality of the sound from your TV - and you’ll be pleasantly surprised by the rich sound it will deliver regardless of what you play through it.

text_fidelity_a:
MAKTAR Qubii Duo USB-C Flash Drive(White Without microSD), Auto Backup While Charging, MFi Certified Compatible with iPhone/iPad/Android, Photo Storage/Stick with File Organizer APP THINGS YOU'LL NEED THAT ARE NOT INCLUDED:
----------------------------------------------------------
1. Your own micro SD card, up to 2tb.
2. A power adapter that has a usb-c port. The Qubii will be plugged into this adapter.
3. A usb-c to usb-c cable. To connect from the Qubii to the usb-c port of your Android phone.
4. A usb-c to Apple lightning if you'll be using an iPhone.

SOME NOTEWORTHY INFO:
---------------------------------
* This is a good idea, now that Google Photos is no longer unlimited.
* It basically backs-up every folder that has an image. There doesn't seem to be a way to choose which folders you want it to back-up. I only need my main camera folder to get backed-up, but oh well, backing up too much is better than too little.
* Once you disconnect from power adapter, you can use the Qubii as OTG storage. You'll need to turn on OTG storage in your system settings. If you have a case on your phone, you'll probably never bother to use it as OTG because you'll need to remove the case.
* Every time you want to transfer files to your PC, NAS, etc., you'll need to remove the micro sd card if your pc doesn't have a usb-c port. My PC does not, so I use a usb to usb-c adapter. This eliminates the hassle of having to take out micro sd cards, dealing with card readers, etc.
* After you transfer everything safely to your pc, if you delete the files on the micro SD card to clear space, the Qubii still maintains its count. So even if these files are still on your phone, it will not re-download them again.

In conclusion, how accurate and precise this system is remains to be seen. So far, it has backed up everything I need it to. I know people complain of missing files, not everything getting backed-up, etc. Most of these complaints revolves around people using iPhones. But we'll see, time will tell. As of now, this is 5-Stars!
text_fidelity_b: MAKTAR Qubii Duo USB-C Flash Drive(White Without microSD), Auto Backup While Charging, MFi Certified Compatible with iPhone/iPad/Android, Photo Storage/Stick with File Organizer APP

Betron EMR90 Foldable Wireless Bluetooth Headphones Over Ear with Microphone Mic Deep Bass There are fortunately many wireless headphones in this price range these days. Usually they are pretty similar, but this is one of the better ones. The first thing I noticed is how SOFT the ear cups are. It feels like something that belongs on a more expensive set, almost luxurious. That makes these much more comfortable to wear for long periods versus many of the other inexpensive headphones. The build quality feels good, and the sound quality is pretty decent too. Speakers of this size are usually pretty good at their bass response, and these are no exception. They naturally have a bit of noise isolation due to the cup design, and you have the option to connect a 3.5mm cable to use them as traditional wired headphones as well.
The one thing I DON'T like, is the microphone. Don't buy these for phone calls. The mic is too far from your mouth to separate you from background noises. Yes, I know airpods also have their mic far from your math but Apple has some sort of magic voodoo to make that work somehow. I've never liked the mic on any of these headphones, so I'm used to that by now. But I feel like these are marketed more for people who want to listen to music, and for that they are great and comfortable! I honestly wish they would disable the handsfree profile so that my phone wouldn't keep trying to use it for phone calls. Otherwise, a solid buy for this price!

Allsop Cool Channel Platform LapDesk for Laptop Notebook Computers (29591) I recently purchased a new laptop. Previously, I owned a netbook, and when I used it on my lap, I simply placed it on a couch pillow. Although my new laptop is still small (it's a [[ASIN:B00DEFW6RI Dell XPS Ultrabook/Tablet]]), it is larger than the netbook, and thus I wanted something a bit more stable for lap use. Unfortunately, most of the lap desks I previewed seemed much too bulky for my purposes.

I was very glad to find the Allsop Cool Channel Platform. First, it fits my new 12.5" laptop perfectly, leaving only about 1/2" on either side. Second, the S-curve design hold the laptop at a very comfortable typing angle. Third, my laptop conveniently tucks into the fold of the "S" for storage--this is how I stow it at night, and this is also offers extra protection when I slip the laptop into an external carry case. I also really like the black/gray color and the sturdy, webbed material.

This platform does have a few (minor) drawbacks. When I type on it, there is a bit of wobble to the stand, as it is very lightweight--a plus, but this also means that the surface is less firm. The other slight issue is that the bottom is a bit on the low slide, making it easy for the laptop to slide around. However, as noted, these are quite minor annoyances which have not been overly problematic for me. I would still recommend this stand, with a final rating of 4 1/2 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Allsop Cool Channel Platform LapDesk for Laptop Notebook Computers (29591)

Jawbone Big JAMBOX Wireless Bluetooth Speaker - Graphite Hex - Retail Packaging The first thing I noticed when I opened the box was how small the Big Jambox is. It's truly portable and the name is more accurate of its sound quality. The first thing I noticed when I turned on the unit was that it talked to me and charted out the steps to pair the speaker to the iPhone 5. The second thing I noticed was the sound. The big full sound. I have truly eclectic tastes. My music collection includes rock, blues, jazz, world music from Africa, the Middle East, and the Lapland of Norway. I listen to didgeridoos from Australia, fiddles, marimbas, and jaw harps from Kyrzykstan. The quality is so good Im a bit blown away by the technology. The clarity is a wonder when listening to vocal qualities of choir ensembles, Bobbie McFerrin, , solo clarinets, and horn sections as well as my favorite twangy African and Middle Eastern instruments. The bass is great considering the speakers size. I predict I will enjoy my symphonic classical music more from now on.
But be reasonable, put it in perspective. Don't expect your Big Jambox to take the place of the power of a live stadium U2 concert or the knock-you -on-your-ass sound wall that passes through your body from a live large brass section of a jazz band orchestra, or be loud enough to overwhelm 10 or 20 loud drunk party goers. Don't be a bonehead! It flabberghasts me that anyone would criticize this speaker. If you actually listen to the sound quality of singers and instruments, or enjoy deep full sounds, spend the money (im on the cheap side) and get the Big Jambox. And dats da facts Jack.
